chapter_theme: The garb of knowledge (ஞான வேடம்): knowledge, not garb, decides; the ignorant in garb go to hell and the knower without it is released. For the Siva-gnani any garb serves, his own garb is Siva-yoga, and he lives as one dead while body and senses remain, silent, released and in Nandi's state.
structure_note: Garb weighed against knowledge (1668 to 1670), the gnani set against ritualists and showy knowers (1671, 1672), and the gnani's own state (1673 to 1675).

1668.reading: Those without knowledge belong to hell even if they wear the garb; those with knowledge are the good released even without it; those who want knowledge go to the Naked One and stand in the garb that has knowledge.
1668.nuance: நக்கன் (the naked one) is Siva, the ascetic beyond all garb, which sharpens the point. The verse does not reject garb: for seekers it is the garb joined to knowledge.

1669.reading: There is no use in those of petty knowledge wearing the garb; those of good knowledge, without wearing it, attain grace; those of evil knowledge, with the stain of sect, and those of lesser knowledge, have nothing to say.
1669.nuance: The four grades (புன், நன், துன், பின் ஞானம்) are a play on one word. பின்ஞானத்தோர் may be those whose knowledge comes later or is secondary, and the last line may mean they cannot speak of the truth at all.

1670.reading: For Siva-gnanis and Siva-yogis the emblems are not futile, if you examine; for the others they are futile; through the four means the peerless reality can come to dwell within.
1670.nuance: அவமாம் அவர்க்கு may refer back to the gnanis (for whom emblems are empty, being unneeded) or to others; the plain and the opposite readings both stand. சாதனம் நான்கும் may be four emblems or the four paths (சரியை, கிரியை, யோகம், ஞானம்), as Siddhanta tradition counts them.

1671.reading: The ritual purifiers wander like a dog at the foot of the stake, the monkey-glad knowers wander pecking about, but the Siva-gnanis wander as men dead while their senses and body remain intact.
1671.nuance: கழுவடி நாய் is read as a dog hanging about the impaling stake for scraps, though கழு may mean washing; குரக்களி ஞானிகள் as knowers with a monkey's restless glee. 'Dead while living' (செத்துத் திரிவர்) is the classic image of the released one whose attachments are gone.

1672.reading: Devotees are devotees; those who are not cannot become devotees nor become that garb; devotees are those who have gained Siva-knowledge, and those who have not are not devotees.
1672.nuance: The verse defines அடியார் by Siva-knowledge, not by garb or by profession of devotion; the repetition of அடியார் in every line drives it home.

1673.reading: For the gnani even a handsome garb is fitting; the garb he has taken is itself Siva-yoga; that garb becomes a means to the knowledge of grace, and for one who is not so, nothing of it avails.
1673.nuance: சுந்தர வேடம் (a beautiful garb) may mean that even rich, unascetic dress does not harm the gnani. The last line can also be read 'for him, whatever comes is fitting and nothing binds'.

1674.reading: The Siva-gnani who reaches the state through knowledge holds a lone temple set in its place; being one of silence he is released and a siddha, and he may be called the other kind of ascetic.
1674.nuance: தானத்தில் வைத்த தனி ஆலயத்தன் may mean his own body or heart is the temple in which the Lord is set, as in 1823. ஏனைத் தவசி could mark him as an ascetic of a different kind from the garb-wearers, or the verse may say only that he too can be called an ascetic.

1675.reading: The state of not being oneself, the becoming Him, the nature that is Siva, the wearing of the seal of attainment and silence: these belong to the one who has gained release at Nandi's feet.
1675.nuance: தான் அன்ற தன்மை and தான் அவன் ஆதல (losing the self and becoming Him) are Siddhanta terms for the soul's union. மேனமும் is unknown; I read it as மோனமும் (silence), which fits 1674.

links.note: 240 says the garb is the true garb for those who keep its way; 1668 goes further, that the knower is released even without it, so the garb is not needed at all where knowledge is.
The same move in another field: the Naladiyar says the beauty of hair and garment is not beauty and learning's is; Tirumular says garb does not save and knowledge does.

source_issues: 1675: line 4 மேனமும் is not a known word; probably மோனமும் (silence).
